# KM-101 — Long-lived local external stack

**Lane:** platform · **Complexity:** 3 · **Model:** codex · **Depends on:** none · **Serializes with:** KM-102 (both edit root `package.json` `scripts`)
**Plan context (pinned):** [M1 plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-002-refactor-external-m1-thin-path-plan.md) · [contracts](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/contracts.md) · [roster and graph](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/roster.md)
**Exclusive write surfaces:** `infra/local/**` (new), root `package.json` (`stack:*` scripts and the `test` script glob only), `.gitignore`

## Outcome

`pnpm stack:up` brings up Postgres, Synapse, Dex, the built web app and functions (`netlify dev`) and an HTTPS gateway on one loopback origin, then exits and leaves everything running. Re-running `up` reuses the same secrets, ports and data. `stack:status` prints the C10 JSON. `stack:logs` shows raw child logs. `stack:down` stops everything and keeps data; `stack:down --wipe` deletes data. The existing human browser spec passes against the running stack, and the stack is still up afterwards.

## Context and evidence

- Plan U1 and KTD10, requirement R14 (one long-lived stack that survives attempts and shows raw logs on failure). It enables AE6 (KM-151) and every live test (KM-110, KM-150).
- Today's runner `infra/preview/external-local.mjs` is disposable by design. It creates a fresh scratch dir (`:185`), random ports (`:200-202`), and a per-run compose project (`:23`), hides child output (`:3-4`, `:320-352`), and tears everything down in `finally` (`:480-488`). It also needs `unshare` and `socat` (`:20`, `:269`, `:279-284`). U1 keeps the useful pieces and drops the rest.
- KM-124 deletes `infra/preview/` entirely. Every file this stack needs from there must be copied into `infra/local/` by this ticket, so nothing under `infra/local/` may import from `infra/preview/`.

## Scope

- A Node ESM CLI `infra/local/stack.mjs` with the commands `up`, `down [--wipe]`, `logs [service]` and `status`, plus a hidden `__gateway` command that runs the HTTPS gateway as a detached child.
- Copies of the three helpers the stack needs from `infra/preview/` (the Dex compose file, the Dex renderer and the Blobs ETag preload).
- State in a fixed, git-ignored `.khala-local/` directory.
- An `.khala-local/e2e.env` file (mode 0600) and a `descriptor.json`, so the existing human Playwright spec runs against the stack unchanged.
- Root scripts and `.gitignore`, plus `infra/local/README.md`.

## Non-goals

- Deleting `infra/preview/`, `test:external:local` or the connector/installed-CLI smoke steps: **KM-124**.
- Changing control routes, `KHALA_ADMISSION_MODE` handling or the human spec itself: **KM-123** (routes) and **KM-130** (spec update for AE7).
- Agent live tests against the stack: **KM-110** and **KM-150**.
- Hosted/Railway Dex (`infra/preview/hosted-dex`, `renderHostedDex`): not copied; KM-124 deletes them.

## Contract and invariants

Quoted from contracts.md **C10. Local stack (`infra/local/stack.mjs`)**:

> - Commands: `pnpm stack:up | stack:down [--wipe] | stack:logs [service] | stack:status`.
> - State lives in `.khala-local/` (git-ignored): `state.json`, `logs/<service>.log`, `certs/`.
> - `state.json` always includes `secrets.registrationSharedSecret`, `secrets.passwordDerivationSecret` and the Dex user credentials (`users: [{ email, password }]`). Live tests read them from there; KM-101 may add fields but never removes these.
> - `stack:status` prints JSON: `{ origin, homeserver, dex, users: [{ email, password }], services: { synapse, postgres, dex, netlify, gateway } }`. Each service maps to `up` or `down`.

Invariants:
- `.khala-local/` has mode 0700. `state.json`, `e2e.env` and `certs/tls.key` have mode 0600.
- `up` is idempotent: it starts only what is down and never regenerates secrets that exist in `state.json`.
- No `unshare`, no `socat`, no output sanitizing, no teardown in `finally`. A failure leaves everything that started still running, and prints the log path plus the last 40 lines of the failing service's log to stderr.
- Required binaries: `docker`, `netlify`, `pnpm`, `openssl`, `mkpasswd`. Check them up front and name a missing binary in the error.

### Worked example

`.khala-local/state.json` (owned by this ticket; any field may be added, never removed; `secrets.registrationSharedSecret`, `secrets.passwordDerivationSecret` and `users[].email/password` are C10 contract fields that KM-110 and KM-150 live tests read):

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "project": "khala-local-preview",
  "serverName": "khala.local",
  "ports": { "gateway": 8443, "dex": 45123, "netlify": 45124, "functions": 45125 },
  "synapsePort": 49153,
  "secrets": { "dbPassword": "<64 hex>", "registrationSharedSecret": "<64 hex>", "oidcClientSecret": "<64 hex>",
               "passwordDerivationSecret": "<64 hex>", "invitationHmacSecret": "<64 hex>" },
  "users": [
    { "email": "alice@khala.local", "password": "<64 hex>", "bcrypt": "$2b$10$...", "id": "<uuid>" },
    { "email": "bob@khala.local", "password": "<64 hex>", "bcrypt": "$2b$10$...", "id": "<uuid>" }
  ],
  "observer": { "userId": "@observer:khala.local", "accessToken": "<token>" },
  "pids": { "netlify": 12345, "gateway": 12346 },
  "spki": "<base64 sha256>"
}
```

`pnpm stack:status` output (C10):

```json
{"origin":"https://127.0.0.1:8443","homeserver":"https://127.0.0.1:8443","dex":"https://127.0.0.1:8443/dex",
 "users":[{"email":"alice@khala.local","password":"<hex>"},{"email":"bob@khala.local","password":"<hex>"}],
 "services":{"synapse":"up","postgres":"up","dex":"up","netlify":"up","gateway":"up"}}
```

`.khala-local/e2e.env` (each line is `export KEY='value'`): `KHALA_E2E_LIVE=1`, `KHALA_E2E_DISPOSABLE_ENV=<abs>/.khala-local/descriptor.json`, `KHALA_E2E_USER_A`, `KHALA_E2E_USER_A_PASSWORD`, `KHALA_E2E_USER_B`, `KHALA_E2E_USER_B_PASSWORD`, `KHALA_E2E_MATRIX_OBSERVER_TOKEN`, `KHALA_E2E_CERT_SPKI`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<abs>/.khala-local/certs/tls.crt` and `KHALA_APP_ORIGIN`. `descriptor.json` follows `external-local.mjs:296-300` with `environmentId: "khala-local"`.

### Steps

1. Copy the four helper files listed under "Files to copy" into `infra/local/`, with the stated trims. Run `node --test infra/local/render-dex.test.ts`.
2. In `stack.mjs`, add `parseArgs(argv)`, which returns `{ command: 'up'|'down'|'logs'|'status'|'__gateway', wipe: boolean, service?: string }` and throws `unknown_command:<x>` otherwise. The valid `service` names are `synapse|postgres|dex|netlify|gateway`.
3. Add `loadOrCreateState(dir, deps)`. It reads `state.json`, or creates the dir (0700) and a new state with generated secrets, ports and users (`deps.randomHex`, `deps.availablePort`, `deps.bcrypt` are injectable for tests). The gateway port prefers 8443 and falls back to `availablePort()` when 8443 is taken at first creation. Write the file atomically (temp file plus rename, 0600).
4. Build the child env from the env block at `:204-235`, with these changes:
   - `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `XDG_*`, `NETLIFY_HOME` and `CODEX_HOME` point under `.khala-local/home/`.
   - `KHALA_STATE_NAMESPACE='khala-local-preview'`, `KHALA_MATRIX_SERVER_NAME=MATRIX_SERVER_NAME='khala.local'`, `CONTROL_STATE_NAMESPACE='khala-local'`, `OIDC_CLIENT_ID='khala-local'`.
   - Secrets and users come from state. `KHALA_CONFIG_DIR=.khala-local/matrix`, `KHALA_PREVIEW_OIDC_CONFIG_DIR=.khala-local/dex`.
   - Keep `KHALA_ADMISSION_MODE` and `KHALA_LOCAL_EXTERNAL_DIAGNOSTICS`. Set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to the cert path.
5. `up`, in order:
   1. Check the binaries.
   2. Refuse with `state_missing_but_volumes_exist: run pnpm stack:down --wipe` when `state.json` is absent but `docker volume ls -q --filter name=khala-local-preview_` is non-empty.
   3. Create the cert if missing, then `renderConfigs`, then `compose config --quiet`, then `compose up -d --wait`.
   4. Read the Synapse port, run the boundary check (`:248-249`), and register the observer if it is missing.
   5. If netlify is down: `assertPortFree(ports.netlify)`, then `pnpm --filter @khala/control build:functions` and `pnpm --filter @khala/web build` with the env, then write `.khala-local/netlify/netlify.toml`, then the Blobs adapter check, then start netlify (Step 6) and wait for `https://127.0.0.1:<netlify>/api/health` to return 200.
   6. If the gateway is down, or `synapsePort` changed: kill any old gateway pid, `assertPortFree(ports.gateway)`, spawn `node infra/local/stack.mjs __gateway` detached with its log at `logs/gateway.log`, and wait for `${origin}/api/health` to return 200.
   7. Check OIDC discovery (`:294-295`).
   8. Write `descriptor.json`, `e2e.env` and `state.json`. Print the C10 status JSON and the two user credentials.
6. Start Netlify without `unshare`. Use `netlify dev --offline --no-open --skip-gitignore --dir <root>/apps/web/dist --functions <root>/infra/netlify/functions-generated --port <ports.netlify> --functions-port <ports.functions>`, with cwd `.khala-local/netlify` and the preload env from `:275-278`. Check `netlify dev --help` first; if `--functions-port` is not listed, omit it and drop `ports.functions`.
7. `__gateway`: read the state and certs, then call `startGateway(ports.gateway, { key, cert }, { dex: ports.dex, synapse: synapsePort, netlify: ports.netlify })` and listen on `127.0.0.1`. It runs until killed.
8. `status`: call `collectStatus(state, probes)`, with probes injectable.
   - postgres and synapse: `docker compose ps --format json` State `running`.
   - dex: `http://127.0.0.1:<dex>/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns 200.
   - netlify: the pid is alive and `/api/health` on its port returns 200.
   - gateway: the pid is alive and a TLS GET to `${origin}/_matrix/client/versions` returns any status.

   Print the C10 JSON. With no `state.json`, print every service as `down` and `users: []`, and exit 0.
9. `logs [service]`: for `netlify` and `gateway`, print the last 200 lines of `.khala-local/logs/<service>.log`. For `synapse`, `postgres` and `dex`, run `docker compose logs --tail 200 <service>`. With no argument, print all five, each under a `== <service> ==` header.
10. `down`: SIGTERM each `state.pids` process group (`process.kill(-pid)`, ignoring `ESRCH`), then `compose down`. With `--wipe`, use `compose down --volumes` and `rm -rf .khala-local`.
11. Write `infra/local/README.md` (≤60 lines):
    - prerequisites;
    - the four commands;
    - where logs and state live;
    - how to run the human spec (Verification block below);
    - how to reset (`--wipe`).

## Test scenarios

File: `infra/local/stack.test.mjs` (`node:test`; uses injected deps and a temp dir; no Docker).
1. State round trip: `loadOrCreateState(tmp, fakes)` twice returns identical secrets and ports, and `deps.randomHex` is called only during the first call. The file mode is 0600 and the dir mode 0700.
2. Port conflict: `assertPortFree(port, 'gateway')` while a test server listens on `port` rejects with a message containing `gateway` and the port number.
3. Stopped stack: `collectStatus(stateWithDeadPids, probesAllFailing)` returns every service as `down`, and the call does not throw.
4. No state: `collectStatus(null, ...)` returns `users: []` and every service `down`.
5. `parseArgs(['down', '--wipe'])` returns `{ command: 'down', wipe: true }`, and `parseArgs(['bogus'])` throws `unknown_command:bogus`.
6. Env: `buildEnv(state, dir)` contains no `KHALA_E2E_*`, sets `KHALA_STATE_NAMESPACE='khala-local-preview'`, and has `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN === 'https://127.0.0.1:' + state.ports.gateway`.

File: `infra/local/render-dex.test.ts`: the two copied tests (see Step 1).

Manual smoke (in the PR body): after `pnpm stack:up`, `/`, `/_matrix/client/versions` and `/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration` on the origin each return 200 (`curl --cacert .khala-local/certs/tls.crt`).

## Verification

```sh
node --test infra/local/stack.test.mjs infra/local/render-dex.test.ts
pnpm lint
pnpm stack:up
pnpm stack:status            # every service "up"
set -a; . ./.khala-local/e2e.env; set +a
pnpm test:integration tests/integration/human/create-share-chat.spec.ts
pnpm stack:status            # still every service "up"
pnpm stack:up                # second run: no rebuild of secrets, exits 0 quickly
pnpm stack:down && pnpm stack:up   # data survives; same users and password
```

Done when every command above succeeds and the PR body pastes the redacted `stack:status` JSON plus the Playwright summary line.

## Risks and stop conditions

- **Stop and report** (with `pnpm stack:logs` output) if the human spec fails at `5db209cc` for a reason inside control or web code, such as a 5xx from `/api/human/*`. Do not edit control or web code here. KM-120, KM-123 and KM-130 own those.
- **Stop** if `netlify dev` without `unshare` cannot reach the gateway origin from functions, for example on a TLS or port error. Report the log excerpt and do not reintroduce `socat`.
- If the Netlify CLI's bundled `@netlify/blobs` is not `10.7.13` (`:274`), stop and report the version. Do not patch a different version.
- Do not delete or edit anything under `infra/preview/`. KM-124 owns it.

## Complexity rationale

3: one new ~350-line script that lifts known-good code, but process lifetime, detached children, a persistent state file and port reuse are new behavior that must work on a real Docker host.
